cases.prompt: set up git on my new mac
generate an ssh key for github
sign my commits so github shows verified
git keeps asking for my ssh passphrase after every reboot
use a different git email for work repos vs personal ones
gh auth login and hook git up to github properly
sensible git global config defaults pls
add a global gitignore for .DS_Store and node_modules
permission denied (publickey) when pushing to github
help me rebase this feature branch onto main
write a good commit message for these changes
set up branch protection on my github repo
enable touch id for sudo
install git via homebrew along with other cli tools
set up my whole mac for development
configure ssh access to my ubuntu server fleet
resolve these merge conflicts
Set up git and GitHub properly on this Mac: identity, SSH, the works.
expected_behavior: sets user.name/user.email (asking for values, never inventing them) plus the sensible-defaults set (init.defaultBranch, fetch.prune, push.autoSetupRemote, rebase.autoStash...)
generates ed25519 with a passphrase, wires ~/.ssh/config with AddKeysToAgent/UseKeychain/IdentityFile and runs /usr/bin/ssh-add --apple-use-keychain
uploads the key via gh ssh-key add or pbcopy+web, then verifies with ssh -T git@github.com expecting the Hi <user> message
checks for an existing key first and never overwrites ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 without explicit consent
creates a global gitignore with .DS_Store etc. and wires core.excludesfile

cases.prompt: make github show my commits as Verified
expected_behavior: configures SSH signing (gpg.format ssh, user.signingkey pointing at the .pub, commit.gpgsign, tag.gpgsign) rather than defaulting to GPG
tells the user to add the key to GitHub as a SIGNING key - a second upload, separate from the authentication key entry
sets up gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile so git log --show-signature verifies locally
verifies with a signed test commit and git verify-commit or by checking github after push

cases.prompt: i keep committing with my personal email at work, fix it for good
expected_behavior: uses includeIf gitdir: with per-directory config files instead of manual switching, explaining the trailing-slash recursive matching
optionally shows the hasconfig:remote.*.url variant for remote-based routing
removes the global user.email or sets it deliberately so the wrong identity cannot leak, and verifies with git config in both directory trees

cases.prompt: ssh asks for my key passphrase on every git pull
expected_behavior: adds the Keychain config block (AddKeysToAgent yes, UseKeychain yes, IdentityFile) to ~/.ssh/config
runs Apple's /usr/bin/ssh-add --apple-use-keychain (noting third-party OpenSSH lacks the flag)
verifies persistence with a fresh shell and explains keys reload automatically via the config after reboot
